title: Re-register Hostinger Tenant Canary workflow under a canonical Actions path

phases.objective: Move the already-reviewed read-only Tenant Canary pull-request workflow to a new canonical Actions path so GitHub registers a fresh workflow identity without changing its name, runner, evidence contract, publisher route, or authority boundary.

e2e_journeys.actor: repository reviewer and GitHub Actions control plane
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The canonical Tenant Canary workflow file and bootstrap contract test
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The workflow is present at one canonical path, retains the exact trusted workflow name and read-only contract, and remains bound to the existing publisher and routing registry.
steps: Remove the prior workflow path from the candidate tree.
Register the same workflow name at the canonical workflow path.
Update the bootstrap contract to read and require the canonical path.
Validate explicit pull-request event types, narrow paths, exact-head checkout, artifact identity, canonical enforcement, and trusted publisher binding.
assertions: Only the workflow path changes; the report contract, runner command, artifact name, and trusted publisher identity remain unchanged.
The PR-head workflow retains contents:read only and persist-credentials:false.
No duplicate prior workflow file remains in the resulting tree.
No runtime module, provider call, credential access, SQL, migration, deployment, Production action, or force push occurs.

phases.objective: Observe the first pull-request-triggered canonical Tenant Canary run and trusted publication after the canonical path reaches main.
Prove stale-head, missing-artifact, malformed-report, and duplicate-workflow-path handling remain fail closed.
Record the first exact-head Hostinger Tenant Canary section on the shared canonical pull-request comment.
This workflow registration change grants no runtime, provider, migration, deployment, or Production authority.
